messages:
prod-bot: [ALERT] 2234567890 - spike in 5xxs and routing fallback chatter. Affected: dedicated pool dp-nyc-3 showing sudden capacity drop; router started routing to regional-variant repeatedly. Pager sent to @anya
anya: taking this. details? which customers impacted?
matt: seeing router logs show fallback policy tripping because dp-nyc-3 reported low available slots. but pool metrics look healthy from node exporter. weird mismatch.
sam: confirm: autoscaler serpentine signal showed a drop-to-zero at 2023-11-07T15:09:xx for dp-nyc-3, then router blackholed ~30% of traffic hitting that pool and fell back to regional variant (eu-west-2) -> higher latencies.
anya: ok paging @dina for customer-impact triage, @leah FYI oncall handoff schedule.
dina: customer success: we have 3 customers reporting elevated 503s (acme-corp, greenleaf, helios). acme reports ~12% request failures since ~15:10 UTC.
matt: grabbing logs. suspected root cause: wrong metric label used by the pool agent. router expects `capacity.available`, pool agent was emitting `capacity.available_nodes` which our router misread as zero due to int->string parsing bug.
ops-bot: automated mitigation suggestion: pause fallback policy for dp-nyc-3 to prevent cross-region oscillation. command: `redwoodctl routing policy pause --pool dp-nyc-3`
anya: I'm going to pause fallback to stop the loop. issuing command now.
anya: ```
$ redwoodctl routing policy pause --pool dp-nyc-3
ok: policy paused for dp-nyc-3
```
matt: verified router stopped issuing new fallbacks within 20s. traffic back to dp-nyc-3, error rate dropping.
sam: still seeing some queued requests dropped earlier. we should scale pool to handle backpressure and adjust autoscaler meanwhile. suggestion: `redwoodctl pool scale dp-nyc-3 --replicas 6`
anya: scaling now.
anya: ```
$ redwoodctl pool scale dp-nyc-3 --replicas 6
scaling: started, expected add 3 replicas
```
leah: quick metrics snapshot (from kube-metrics):
```
router.fallback_rate: 78% -> 3% after policy pause
dp-nyc-3.errors.5xx: 220/min -> 18/min
dp-nyc-3.capacity_signal (agent): 0.0 (string)
dp-nyc-3.nodes_ready: 6
```
matt: yes that capacity_signal being `0.0` as a string caused our YAML parsing to coerce into falsey and router treated pool as drained. patch ready to fix agent label parsing; will push hotfix to pool-agent config after stabilization.
anya: customer-impact: acme got degraded for 25 minutes, we should offer status update and credit. Dina liaise with account.
dina: will message acme and greenleaf with incident ETA. prepping short blurb.
leah: I'm taking the second shift for follow-up. leaving actions: 1) roll agent parsing hotfix (matt) 2) revert fallback policy pause only after verifying hotfix in canary (anya+matt) 3) postmortem draft (leah) 4) customer comms (dina).
matt: starting hotfix deploy to canary pool now. patch changes parse numeric tokens and validate presence of `capacity.available`.
matt: ```
- change: agent -> emit `capacity.available` as int
- change: router -> validate label exists before fallback
```
ops-bot: deployment tracker: canary deploy started at 15:45 UTC to dp-nyc-3-canary.
anya: we'll leave fallback paused until canary proves stable for 30m. If no regressions, we'll resume and roll.
leah: handoff done. I'll monitor until 16:30 UTC then update postmortem skeleton in the channel. please annotate any logs/commands used. :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks team. main mitigations: pause fallback policy, scale pool, deploy agent parsing fix. follow-ups documented.
prod-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, impact reduced. severity -> reduced to SEV3. will reopen if errors spike.
leah: assigning owner for postmortem: @matt (root cause), @anya (mitigation timeline), @dina (customer impact), @leah (writeup).
